capability.summary: Return one instantaneous virtual-memory and swap snapshot
capability.description: Calls psutil.virtual_memory() and psutil.swap_memory() once and emits current host/container memory counters in a JSON envelope. It accepts no arguments and does not monitor over time.
capability.problem_space: Point-in-time operating-system memory telemetry for the runtime environment; not continuous monitoring, process profiling, leak detection, capacity forecasting, alerting, cleanup, or memory reservation.

env_requirements: psutil Python package with access to runtime memory statistics
constraint.io_signature: Input: none; command-line arguments are ignored. Output: one JSON envelope containing virtual_memory and swap byte counters plus percent-used values at the instant sampled.
constraint.output_shape: Success: {status: "success", tool: "psutil", virtual_memory: {total_bytes: integer, available_bytes: integer, used_bytes: integer, free_bytes: integer, percent_used: number}, swap: {total_bytes: integer, used_bytes: integer, percent_used: number}}, exit 0. psutil or platform-access failures are uncaught and may traceback without JSON.
limitations: values are nondeterministic point-in-time host or container measurements and can change immediately after sampling
takes no path or directory input; filesystem file/directory boundaries are not applicable to this snapshot tool
does not sample repeatedly, set thresholds, emit alerts, identify processes, free RAM, modify swap, or predict capacity
platform accounting semantics for available, used, free, and swap vary; no timeout or fallback is implemented

output_contract.description: JSON envelope containing one instantaneous virtual-memory and swap snapshot from psutil.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: get a virtual memory and swap snapshot
negative_intents: continuously monitor memory or emit alerts
profile a process or detect memory leaks
free allocate or reserve system memory
